rule_findings.title: Successful login at unusual hour
rule_findings.description: carol logged in from 10.0.7.77 at 03:14. Review indicator, not proof of compromise.

rule_findings.title: Suspicious login linked to large download
rule_findings.description: Suspicious login by carol from 10.0.7.77 followed by a 52,428,800-byte download within 1 hour. Correlation alone does not prove exfiltration.

summary: The scenario involves a suspicious login by carol from 10.0.7.77 at 03:14 followed by a large HTTP response. The correlation between the login and the download is a high severity finding, while the large response is a low severity finding.

attack_chain.explanation: The login by carol at 03:14 is correlated with a large HTTP response to /exports/customers_full.csv.
The server returned a large HTTP response to the login IP.

mitigations: Implement rate limiting for SSH login attempts to detect and block suspicious activity.
Configure access controls for the /exports directory to restrict access to authorized users only.
Enable SSL/TLS encryption for all HTTP traffic to prevent data exfiltration over unencrypted channels.
Audit and monitor SSH login logs for unusual patterns or deviations from normal behavior.
Review and update the server's security policies to ensure that only authorized users have access to sensitive data.
